_comment: Wonders of the world drawn on the map (MapView, art/wonders/<id>.svg) at their real places (lon, lat). kind: natural, man_made, or ancient (the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World now lost, drawn as they were, faded; the Great Pyramid, the one still standing, is man_made). km: its size in the world (exaggerated so it reads), drawn growing and shrinking with the map; line (for a few): the course it follows, drawn along it. tier: how famous (1 most), kept for reference. when: when it was built, formed or is to be seen. Picked from the New 7 Wonders of the World, the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, the Seven Natural Wonders, the New 7 Wonders of Nature and other world-famous landmarks. Clicking one opens its popup and checks it off in the field guide's Wonders tab. night_lights (optional): lamps that glow at night over the picture, each [x, y, size (all shares of the picture, 0 to 1, from its top left), colour (hex), brightness] (MapView._draw_wonder_lights()).

wonders.name: Great Pyramid of Giza
wonders.fact: Built for the pharaoh Khufu from some 2.3 million stone blocks, it was the tallest building on Earth for nearly 4,000 years, and it's the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing.

wonders.name: Great Wall of China
wonders.when: Built from the 7th century BC to the 1600s
wonders.fact: All its walls, trenches and ramparts together run over 21,000 km across northern China; most of what stands today, like this stretch at Badaling, is Ming dynasty brickwork. Despite the legend, it can't be seen from the Moon with the naked eye.

wonders.name: Statue of Liberty
wonders.fact: A gift from the people of France, she greeted millions of immigrants sailing into New York Harbor. Her copper skin, about as thick as two pennies, turned from shiny brown to green within about 30 years.

wonders.name: Colosseum
wonders.fact: The largest amphitheatre ever built held some 50,000 people for gladiator fights and wild animal hunts; it could even be flooded for mock sea battles in its early years.

wonders.name: Taj Mahal
wonders.fact: The emperor Shah Jahan built this white marble tomb for his wife Mumtaz Mahal. Some 20,000 workers built it, and its marble seems to change color from pink at dawn to white at noon and gold by moonlight.

wonders.name: Christ the Redeemer
wonders.fact: The 30 m statue stands with its arms 28 m wide atop Corcovado, 700 m above Rio de Janeiro. It's made of reinforced concrete covered in thousands of small soapstone tiles, and it's struck by lightning several times a year.

wonders.name: Machu Picchu
wonders.fact: This Inca citadel sits on a ridge 2,430 m up in the Andes. Its stones were cut so precisely that they fit without mortar, and the Spanish conquerors never found it; the wider world learned of it in 1911.

wonders.name: Chichén Itzá
wonders.fact: The great Maya pyramid El Castillo has 365 steps, one for each day of the year. At the spring and autumn equinoxes, the setting sun casts a shadow like a serpent slithering down its stairs.

wonders.name: Petra
wonders.fact: The Nabataeans carved this city straight into rose-red sandstone cliffs and grew rich on the incense trade. Its most famous facade, the Treasury, is reached through a narrow gorge over a kilometer long.

wonders.name: Eiffel Tower
wonders.fact: Meant to stand for only 20 years, it was saved because it was useful as a radio mast. It's repainted by hand every seven years or so, with about 60 tonnes of paint, and grows up to 15 cm taller on hot summer days.

wonders.name: Sydney Opera House
wonders.fact: Its shells, inspired by the segments of a peeled orange, are covered with over a million self-cleaning white and cream tiles. It took 14 years to build and cost about 15 times its first estimate.

wonders.name: Stonehenge
wonders.fact: Its great sarsen stones weigh around 25 tonnes each, and its smaller bluestones were dragged some 240 km from the Preseli Hills in Wales. It's lined up with the sunrise at the summer solstice.

wonders.name: Angkor Wat
wonders.fact: The largest religious monument in the world was built as a Hindu temple to Vishnu and became Buddhist. Its five towers stand for the peaks of Mount Meru, and it's on Cambodia's flag.

wonders.name: Moai of Easter Island
wonders.fact: The Rapa Nui people carved nearly 1,000 of these giant heads from volcanic rock and moved them across the island, perhaps by 'walking' them upright with ropes. Most face inland, watching over their villages.

wonders.name: Parthenon
wonders.fact: The temple to Athena on the Acropolis of Athens has no truly straight lines: its columns bulge slightly and lean inwards, so that from below it looks perfectly straight.

wonders.name: Golden Gate Bridge
wonders.fact: For decades the longest suspension bridge in the world, it's painted International Orange so that it shows up in San Francisco's famous fog.

wonders.name: Burj Khalifa
wonders.fact: At 828 m it's the tallest building in the world. You can watch the sunset from the ground, then ride up and watch it again from the top.

wonders.name: Mount Rushmore
wonders.fact: The faces of Presidents Washington, Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt and Lincoln are each about 18 m high, carved into granite mostly with dynamite.

wonders.name: Sagrada Família
wonders.fact: Antoni Gaudí's basilica in Barcelona has been under construction for over 140 years. Gaudí worked on it for 43 years, saying, 'My client is not in a hurry.'

wonders.name: Hagia Sophia
wonders.fact: Built as the cathedral of Constantinople, it was the largest church in the world for nearly a thousand years. Its vast dome seems to float on a ring of 40 windows.

wonders.name: St Basil's Cathedral
wonders.fact: Ivan the Terrible built it on Moscow's Red Square to celebrate the capture of Kazan. Its nine chapels are crowned with onion domes, each painted differently.

wonders.name: Hanging Gardens of Babylon
wonders.when: Said to be built about 600 BC; long gone
wonders.fact: Said to be built by King Nebuchadnezzar II for his homesick wife, the terraced gardens were watered by machines lifting water from the Euphrates. No trace has ever been found, and some think they stood in Nineveh instead, or never existed at all.

wonders.name: Temple of Artemis
wonders.fact: This huge marble temple at Ephesus was burned down in 356 BC by a man who wanted to be famous, on the night, legend says, that Alexander the Great was born. It was rebuilt even grander, and one column has been put back up today.

wonders.name: Statue of Zeus at Olympia
wonders.when: Made about 435 BC; lost in the 5th century AD
wonders.fact: The sculptor Phidias made this seated Zeus, about 12 m tall, of ivory and gold over a wooden frame. It was said that if Zeus stood up, he would have gone through the temple's roof.

wonders.name: Mausoleum at Halicarnassus
wonders.when: Built about 350 BC; fell by the 15th century
wonders.fact: The tomb of Mausolus, a Persian governor, was so grand that his name became our word for any great tomb: mausoleum. Earthquakes brought it down, and crusaders used its stones to build Bodrum Castle.

wonders.name: Colossus of Rhodes
wonders.fact: This bronze statue of the sun god Helios stood about 33 m tall over the harbor of Rhodes, but an earthquake toppled it after only 54 years. Despite the famous pictures, it almost certainly didn't straddle the harbor entrance.

wonders.name: Lighthouse of Alexandria
wonders.when: Built about 280 BC; fell in the 14th century
wonders.fact: Standing on the island of Pharos, about 100 m tall, it guided ships into Alexandria with a fire by night and a mirror by day for over 1,500 years. 'Pharos' still means lighthouse in many languages.

wonders.name: Grand Canyon
wonders.when: Carved over the last 5 to 6 million years
wonders.fact: The Colorado River cut this canyon up to 1.8 km deep and 29 km wide. The rocks at its bottom are nearly 2 billion years old, almost half the age of the Earth.

wonders.name: Great Barrier Reef
wonders.when: Grown over the last 20,000 years or so
wonders.fact: The largest structure built by living things stretches some 2,300 km along Queensland and can be seen from space. It's made of nearly 3,000 separate reefs, home to over 1,500 kinds of fish.

wonders.name: Mount Everest
wonders.when: Still rising, a few millimeters a year
wonders.fact: At 8,849 m, the highest mountain above sea level. It was first climbed by Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay in 1953, and there are fossils of sea creatures near its summit.

wonders.name: Victoria Falls
wonders.when: Highest in the rainy season, February to May
wonders.fact: The Zambezi River plunges over 100 m along a front 1,708 m wide, making it the largest sheet of falling water in the world. Its local name, Mosi-oa-Tunya, means 'the smoke that thunders'.

wonders.name: Harbor of Rio de Janeiro
wonders.when: Formed by the sea flooding a river valley
wonders.fact: Guanabara Bay, ringed by granite peaks like Sugarloaf Mountain, is one of the largest natural bays in the world. The Portuguese who sailed in on 1 January 1502 thought it was a river's mouth, and named it the River of January: Rio de Janeiro.

wonders.name: Northern Lights
wonders.when: Seen on dark nights, September to March
wonders.fact: The aurora borealis glows when particles from the Sun hit the upper atmosphere, about 100 to 300 km up: oxygen shines green and red, nitrogen blue and purple. It's brightest in a ring around the magnetic pole, over Lapland, Iceland, Canada and Alaska.

wonders.name: Parícutin
wonders.fact: This volcano was born in a farmer's cornfield on 20 February 1943, while he watched. It grew 336 m in its first year and buried two villages before it fell silent in 1952.

wonders.name: Amazon Rainforest
wonders.fact: The largest rainforest on Earth covers about 5.5 million km² across nine countries, home to around one in ten of all known species. The Amazon River carries a fifth of all the river water flowing into the world's oceans.

wonders.name: Ha Long Bay
wonders.fact: Around 1,600 limestone islands and islets rise sheer from the emerald water, many hollowed into caves. Its name means 'where the dragon descends': legend says a dragon made the islands to fend off invaders.

wonders.name: Iguazu Falls
wonders.fact: About 275 waterfalls stretch nearly 3 km along the edge of a lava plateau. On seeing them, Eleanor Roosevelt is said to have exclaimed, 'Poor Niagara!'

wonders.name: Jeju Island
wonders.when: Built by eruptions over 2 million years
wonders.fact: A volcanic island crowned by Hallasan, South Korea's highest mountain, with lava tubes running for kilometers underground. Its haenyeo, women free divers, have gathered seafood from its waters for centuries.

wonders.name: Komodo
wonders.when: Dragons on the islands for about 1 million years
wonders.fact: Komodo and its neighboring islands are the only home of the Komodo dragon, the largest lizard in the world at up to 3 m long, with a venomous bite.

wonders.name: Puerto Princesa Underground River
wonders.when: Carved in limestone over millions of years
wonders.fact: The river winds 8.2 km through a cave under a limestone mountain on Palawan before flowing straight into the sea. Boats can paddle in for over 4 km, past stalactites and colonies of bats.

wonders.name: Table Mountain
wonders.when: Its rocks are about 600 million years old
wonders.fact: Its flat top, 3 km across, rises over 1,000 m above Cape Town. When cloud spills over its edge like a tablecloth, locals say the devil and a pirate are having a smoking contest.

wonders.name: Niagara Falls
wonders.fact: Over 2,800 tonnes of water pour over the falls every second. The falls have worn their way back about 11 km since the last ice age, and people have gone over them in barrels.

wonders.name: Mount Fuji
wonders.fact: Japan's highest mountain, at 3,776 m, is a near-perfect volcanic cone, snow-capped for much of the year. Climbing it is a summer pilgrimage, and hundreds of thousands reach the top each year.

wonders.name: Mount Kilimanjaro
wonders.when: Formed about a million years ago
wonders.fact: At 5,895 m, the highest mountain in Africa and the tallest that stands on its own. Though it's near the equator, it has glaciers on top, now shrinking fast.

wonders.name: Uluru
wonders.fact: This sandstone monolith rises 348 m from the desert and glows red at sunrise and sunset. It's sacred to the Aṉangu people, whose land it is, and most of it lies hidden underground.

wonders.name: Angel Falls
wonders.when: Fullest in the rainy season, June to November
wonders.fact: The highest waterfall in the world drops 979 m from a flat-topped mountain, so far that much of the water turns to mist before it reaches the bottom. It's named after Jimmie Angel, a pilot who flew over it in 1933.

wonders.name: Yellowstone
wonders.when: Old Faithful erupts every hour or two
wonders.fact: The world's first national park sits on a supervolcano, with over half of all the world's geysers. Old Faithful shoots boiling water up to 56 m into the air.

wonders.name: Salar de Uyuni
wonders.when: A giant mirror in the rainy season, January to March
wonders.fact: The world's largest salt flat covers over 10,000 km², so flat that satellites use it to check their altimeters. After rain, a thin layer of water turns it into a mirror of the sky.

wonders.name: Giant's Causeway
wonders.fact: About 40,000 interlocking basalt columns, most of them six-sided, step down into the sea where lava cooled and cracked. Legend says the giant Finn McCool built it to cross to Scotland.
